brief.issue: a fracture missed on X-ray at an emergency department and the patient sent home as a sprain

items.title: Failure to conduct an adequate medical assessment and to order an x-ray — Health & Disability Commissioner
items.quote: The Commissioner found that by failing to conduct an adequate medical assessment that took full account of the woman’s symptoms, and by not obtaining an X-ray of her hip, the doctor failed to provide services with reasonable care and skill and breached Right 4(1)
items.why: An HDC finding of breach of Right 4(1) where inadequate assessment and no X-ray delayed identification of a fracture, though not shown to involve this provider.

items.title: Failure to conduct an adequate medical assessment and to order an x-ray — Health & Disability Commissioner
items.quote: Had an adequate examination of Mrs A’s hip occurred, a more accurate clinical picture would have emerged, and Mrs A’s fracture may have been identified earlier.
items.why: This HDC passage says earlier adequate examination might have identified the fracture earlier, but the quote itself does not show the outcome and is not tied to this provider.

items.title: Care of woman with hand injury — Health & Disability Commissioner
items.quote: Accordingly, Dr C did not provide services to Ms A with reasonable care and skill, and so breached Right 4(1) of the Code of Health and Disability Services Consumers' Rights (the Code).
items.why: An HDC case summary finding a breach of Right 4(1) about care for a hand injury, but it is not shown to involve Te Toka Tumai Auckland.
